The Slow Decay of Link Rot

By Dana Okonkwo

A link that worked in 2011 has roughly even odds of working today, and the odds get worse every year. The web does not so much forget as quietly replace what was there with something else, usually a parking page or a redirect to a homepage that has no idea what you were looking for.

The failure is rarely dramatic. Domains lapse, content management systems are migrated, and the new one does not preserve the old permalink structure. Each individual decision is reasonable. The aggregate effect is that a decade of citations quietly stops resolving, and nobody is responsible for it.

Archiving is the only durable answer, and it has to happen at the moment of reading rather than at the moment you notice the link is gone. By then the content is already unavailable and no amount of diligence recovers it.
